ArXiv cs.AI.title: LRMoE: Demand-Side Load Re-Calibration for Efficient MoE Training on Memory-Constrained Nodes
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2610.37720v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models offer scalable capacity for Web applications, but uneven routing creates computation and communication bottlenecks. Existing placement and replication methods redistribute this workload, yet additional expert copies compete with token-related buffers for limited GPU memory. We present LRMoE, a memory-aware MoE training system that jointly recalibrates backward demand and balances the retained workload. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Amortized Localized Posterior Inference for Model Calibration with Application to an Ocean Turbulence Closure
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2610.37731v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Model discrepancy may prevent a single calibration parameter from reproducing a physical response across the context domain. In addition, uncertainties in observations and contexts affect calibration and must be accounted for and quantified. We construct a family of localized posteriors by weighting observation likelihoods according to their proximity to a target context. ArXiv cs.AI.title: ThinkJev: One Thought, Every Budget for Calibrated Typed Decisions
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2610.37732v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Many uses of language models end in a typed decision: a choice among a closed set of options, whose probabilities code can act on. Reading those probabilities from one forward pass is fast but often wrong on decisions that take several steps, such as arithmetic, counting, and date comparison. Letting the model think first fixes most of these errors, but costs seconds per decision instead of milliseconds. ArXiv cs.AI.title: OpenFrontiers: A Collection of Open Research Problems and a Benchmark for Scientific Rediscovery
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2610.37739v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown increasing promise in research-level problem solving, yet a comprehensive collection of such problems is still missing, and evaluating them on research-level problems remains challenging. We introduce OpenFrontiers, a cross-disciplinary resource that combines a structured corpus of open research problems with a retrospective benchmark of recently resolved problems in mathematics. ArXiv cs.AI.title: WebAnything: From the Wild Web to Scalable Agent Environments
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2610.37786v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Web agents require diverse, executable, and resettable website environments for reproducible training and evaluation. Human-assisted mirrors demand per-site engineering, while generative construction can diverge from specified real websites. Capture-and-replay preserves observations, with interaction coverage constrained by captured content and replay capabilities.
  We present WebAnything, a fully automated framework that reconstructs source-grounded, reusable Web environments from real URLs without per-site manual implementation or repair afte

ArXiv cs.AI.title: What Does an Ontology Catch? Curated, LLM-Generated and Data-Derived Ontologies as Checkers of LLM Agents over Knowledge Graphs
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2610.37809v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM agents that answer questions over Web knowledge graphs are increasingly wrapped in checks derived from the graph's ontology, on the assumption that a formal schema makes a reliable judge. Yet a checker can be wrong as well: it can miss errors, and it can flag correct answers and push the agent into "fixing" them. Whether a curated ontology is worth its cost as such a judge, and how it compares with an ontology an LLM writes or a schema mined from the data, is unknown. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Measuring Where Intent Gets Lost in Agentic Smart Contract Synthesis
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2610.37830v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AI agents can now write software from a plain-English description, but code that runs is not the same as code that does what was asked. This gap matters most for smart contracts, the programs behind Web3 applications that move money on a blockchain and cannot be fixed once deployed. We ask how to check whether an AI-written contract behaves as it should, and where the requested behavior gets lost.

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Detecting Covert Collusion between AI Agents through Partner-Outsider Positive Listening
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2610.37849v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AI agents that share a secret convention can coordinate through messages that look innocent, so a monitor that reads only the messages can miss them. We propose a behavioural test: a partner that uses a code reacts to the exact wording of a message, whereas an uninvolved agent placed in its seat does not. Partner--Outsider Positive Listening (PoPLi) is the difference between the two agents in how much their action changes when the message is reworded with its meaning kept, and it is computed after the fact by replaying logged prompts. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Evaluating and improving AI agents for sequencing protocol understanding
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2610.37851v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Existing scientific-agent benchmarks rarely evaluate whether agents can reconstruct the exact molecular structures and generation workflows specified by sequencing protocols, a capability critical for analyzing customized sequencing assays. We introduce LibStructBench, a document-grounded benchmark for reconstructing sequencing-library structures and molecular workflows. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Seq@K: Evaluating Language Models Under Sequential Feedback
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2610.37859v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Language-model agents differ fundamentally from prior intelligent systems in their ability to learn from natural language in context. This capability enables agents to iteratively refine their answers in response to feedback, a prevalent mode of operation in modern agentic workflows. However, the community primarily ranks models by metrics such as Pass@1 or Pass@K, which cannot capture how they utilize feedback on prior attempts. ArXiv cs.AI.title: What Constitutes Food Similarity? Visual Representations and Retrieval in Indian Cuisine
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2610.37867v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Food similarity underlies retrieval, recommendation, substitution, and other food computing tasks, yet food representations are typically evaluated by identity preservation. We ask what happens to food similarity beyond identity: how different visual representations organize foods into relational neighborhoods, what culinary relationships these neighborhoods reveal or obscure, and how consistently these structures emerge across representations. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Verification Learning Theory: A Process Model of Checking and Retention in AI-Assisted Judgment
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2610.37875v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Accurate AI assistance can improve immediate judgments while reducing opportunities to practise the operations needed for independent performance. Verification Learning Theory (VLT) formalises this possibility for claim-evaluation practice followed by correct, independent, rule-specific feedback. The model links perceived assistant reliability to evidence checking and links the history of those checks to retained rule use. ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2610.37896v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Subjective judgments such as offensiveness often vary substantially across individuals, motivating pluralistic modeling approaches that incorporate annotators' socio-demographic information to capture this variation. However, prior findings on the benefits of socio-demographic information for pluralistic modeling are mixed, calling for a systematic analysis of both its effectiveness and the mechanisms through which it improves prediction. ArXiv cs.AI.title: FilingLoop: Evaluating and Evolving LLM Agents for Corporate Disclosure Review and Revision
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2610.37905v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Public disclosure repositories such as SEC EDGAR support informed investment through web access to corporate filings. Supporting their review with language model agents requires discovering unstated deficiencies across related documents, acquiring missing company facts, and verifying that requested revisions satisfy evidence-backed requirements. Existing financial question-answering evaluations provide limited evidence of these interactive capabilities. We introduce \textbf{FilingLoop}, an interactive benchmark and a self-evolving agent framewor

ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2610.37906v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Spiking reservoir computing combines the training efficiency of fixed recurrent reservoirs with the energy efficiency of event-driven inference, where computation is triggered by sparse spikes rather than executed densely at every timestep. However, existing spiking reservoirs almost exclusively rely on Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) neurons, whose low-pass dynamics limit their ability to distinguish information encoded at different temporal frequencies. ArXiv cs.LG.title: Moment-Guided Optimizers for Noisy Deep Learning: MGO-SC as a Simple Consistency Gate for Adam-Style Updates
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2610.37712v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Adaptive optimizers are widely used in deep learning, yet their behavior can degrade under heavy stochasticity and label noise where the sign and magnitude of gradients can be unstable. We study MGO-SC (Moment-Guided Optimizer with Sign-Consistency), a lightweight modification of Adam-style methods that derives a coordinate-wise consistency gate from the magnitude of a sign exponential moving average (EMA): coordinates whose gradient sign is stable are trusted, while coordinates whose sign fluctuates are down-weighted. ArXiv cs.LG.title: What a Weight Update Buys: Leverage Across Training Stages
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2610.37719v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Post-training moves a language model's weights by about a thousandth of their norm and changes its behavior sharply; pretraining moves them by a third and buys a slow drift. We introduce leverage, an exact measure of what a unit of weight change buys: the Fisher quadratic form of an update, computed with one forward-mode pass per direction, divided by the same form for random directions of the same size at the same checkpoint. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2610.37726v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Accurate regression need not yield the correct equation after support selection. For a median/sample-standard-deviation threshold in neural PDE discovery, we derive an exact two-signal retention boundary and a complete-vector perturbation bound. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2610.37727v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In machine learning, symbolic reasoning approaches often rely on static architectures that hinder integration into deep neural networks and gradient-based optimization. To address this, we introduce the Native Predicate Neuron, a differentiable logic-reasoning neural module that enriches standard architectures with symbolic reasoning capabilities via first-order logic quantization. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2610.37733v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This work studies context-aware selective transfer learning for multi-well groundwater anomaly forecasting in the Netherlands. Source-domain pretraining can raise average accuracy but is not uniformly reliable: it degrades performance on a substantial fraction of heterogeneous wells. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2610.37737v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Prior-Data Fitted Networks (PFNs) replace the hyperparameter refitting of Gaussian Process (GP) surrogates in Bayesian optimisation with a single forward pass, at the cost of a prior that is fixed at meta-training time. We show empirically that a PFN's predictive log-likelihood falls increasingly behind that of a refitted GP as the objective function's lengthscale grows beyond the mode of the PFN's meta-training prior, and that this deficit carries over to optimisation performance. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2610.37796v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent work has hypothesised that large language models may represent some concepts as multi-dimensional manifolds instead of single directions. Using these manifolds to interpret or steer representations often assumes that moving along them corresponds to a continuous change in the represented concept. In this work, we test this continuous manifold assumption on the prototypical weekday manifold. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2610.37819v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Quantum machine learning (QML) is increasingly explored for medical classification, yet its behaviour under subgroup-aware fairness criteria remains understudied. We present an empirical fairness audit of classical and quantum classifiers for medical imaging, assuming QML is not inherently fair. Two scenarios are evaluated: dermatological lesions on DDI (sensitive attribute: Fitzpatrick skin type) and chest X-rays on CheXpert-derived data (sensitive attribute: age group). ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2610.37823v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Event cameras, spiking cochleas and similar sensors emit asynchronous events, yet most learning systems first bin them into frames or packets, so the output depends on how the stream was sliced. Networks whose state is updated exactly at every event and evolves in closed form between events are invariant to this slicing. arXiv:2610.37828v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: An AI developer often has several candidate versions of a system and can deploy a mixture of them, sending each request to a randomly chosen version, as in A/B testing. Each stakeholder (e.g., a safety team, a regulator, or a customer with private test data) accepts a mixture exactly when its expected performance (e.g., its rate of harmful replies) meets the stakeholder's own standard, which the developer can learn only by asking whether a proposed mixture is acceptable. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2610.37833v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Modern automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems have achieved remarkable accuracy by scaling model depth and capacity, but at the cost of increased memory, energy, and computational demands. On edge devices where ASR is often most needed, such as watches and glasses, deploying such large models is infeasible due to extremely constrained resources. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2610.37842v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As growing compute budgets outpace the growth of high-quality training data, large language models must be trained with both compute and data constraints in mind. Unfortunately, existing prescriptions for data-constrained scaling suffer from two important limitations. First, past works hold key hyperparameters such as weight decay fixed with scale, despite the fact that optimal hyperparameters vary wildly with model size and number of epochs. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2610.37880v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Equation learning seeks to discover compact, interpretable equations from data using various machine-learning techniques. However, few workflows discover and interpret learned equations in sparse, high-dimensional materials datasets. We present nn-EQL, an equation-learning framework that generates candidate equations through iterative training, pruning, and retraining of a neural network with customizable, user-specified neuron-level activation functions. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2610.37898v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Graph Contrastive Learning (GCL) has achieved remarkable success in self-supervised representation learning by maximizing agreement between augmented views of a graph. ArXiv cs.LG.description:

The Verge AI.description: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic say they will adopt a new standard that publishers can use to opt out of being scraped by AI, as reported earlier by Search Engine Roundtable. With this control, publishers can apply their AI training preferences across multiple AI companies, instead of setting them individually. The shared "policy token" signal […]

The Verge AI.title: Google’s satellite AI server transmits its first response to Earth
The Verge AI.description: Google's AI chip-equipped satellite has generated its first response from space. The Verge AI.title: Starbucks wants to use AI to show you a ‘personalized digital menu’ at the drive-thru
The Verge AI.description: Starbucks could eventually show you a personalized digital menu when you pull up to the drive-thru. The Verge AI.description: Pope Leo XIV says AI systems should be "disarmed," adding that humans "have the responsibility to guide, change and, when necessary, reject its applications." In Friday's Papal Address, Pope Leo encourages United Nations member states to "take concrete steps toward banning lethal autonomous weapons" during their meeting in Geneva next month. The Verge AI.title: Maine’s data center revolt will decide who controls the Senate
The Verge AI.description: Maine Sen. Susan Collins, a Republican, was midway through defending her record during the final debate of the midterms when an audience member cut her short. The Verge AI.title: Wikipedia’s operator says a bad AI copyright ruling could threaten the open web
The Verge AI.description: The Wikimedia Foundation is staking out a middle ground in a group of landmark AI copyright cases, pushing courts to legally protect large language models (LLMs) training on copyrighted work - but not chatbots regurgitating that work to users. An overly black-and-white ruling, it says, could either deprive Wikipedians of useful AI-based tools or endanger […]

The Verge AI.description: Now you can generate, preview, and edit PDFs, Google Docs, Google Sheets, slide decks, Markdown files, TXT files, and code directly within Google Gemini. Wired AI.title: How a Contractor’s Claude Agent Got Into the Pentagon
Wired AI.description: This week on “Uncanny Valley,” we discuss the contractor who plugged their AI agent into a Pentagon system, Anthropic’s IPO filing, and the volunteers gearing up to counter ICE at the midterms.

Wired AI.title: A Defense Contractor Gave Their Personal AI Agent Access to a Secure Pentagon System
Wired AI.description: Sources tell WIRED that an Accenture employee’s personal Claude agent ran on a DOD network for two months before it was identified and the vulnerability could be patched.

Wired AI.title: The ‘Pain in the Ass’ Math That Could Save Vibe Coding From Itself
Wired AI.description: A new startup called &Truth is joining the race to automate formal verification, a painstaking process that uses math to prove software works as intended.

Wired AI.title: Mistral Says Its AI Model ‘Le Chonk’ Has Leapfrogged China in the Open-Weight Race
Wired AI.description: The French AI lab claims its latest release matches or outperforms even the best models from DeepSeek and Z.ai in coding and cybersecurity.

Wired AI.title: I Gave My Blood to the AI Death Clock
Wired AI.description: Death Clock promises to predict when you’re going to die and help you extend your time on Earth. After a month, I felt like it was sucking the life out of me.

Wired AI.title: I Put a Bunch of AI Agents in Charge of a Fantasy Soccer Team. They’re Not Better Than Humans—Yet
Wired AI.description: To experiment with AI’s predictive skills, I let Codex loose on a fantasy team. It tried to bench Erling Haaland at first, but it soon learned the error of its ways.

Wired AI.title: Macmillan Staff Say the Publisher Threw a Party for a Workplace AI Assistant That Was Later Killed
Wired AI.description: Workers tell WIRED that NOA—or “No Ordinary Assistant”—was unhelpful. Bestselling authors also say AI is ruining their relationships with Big Five publishers.

Wired AI.title: AI Emergency Alerts Are Coming. Humans Might Not Be Ready
Wired AI.description: Human beings struggle with emergency communication. Chatbots can help—if people take them seriously.

Wired AI.title: Should AI Decide Your Court Case? This Judge Says Yes
Wired AI.description: One of England’s top judges, Geoffrey Vos, believes that AI could adjudicate plenty of civil cases. The question, he says, is where the line should be drawn.

Wired AI.title: Anthropic Says It Will Revolutionize Biology—Some Day
Wired AI.description: In breathless press releases and posts, the company has touted its models’ ability to deliver scientific breakthroughs. But its IPO filing taps the brakes on just how fast its AI will lead to big discoveries.

MIT News — AI.title: MIT affiliates named 2026 Schmidt Sciences AI2050 Fellows
MIT News — AI.description: Five MIT faculty members and two additional alumni are honored with fellowships to advance research on beneficial AI.

MIT News — AI.title: Q&A: Hey AI, who should I vote for this year?
MIT News — AI.description: MIT professors Adam Berinsky and Chara Podimata discuss a new project to track how AI chatbots are responding to questions about the 2026 U.S. midterm elections.

MIT News — AI.title: 3 Questions: Why infrastructure is entering a defining era
MIT News — AI.description: Professor Ali Jadbabaie describes how AI, digital transformation, climate change, and complex geopolitics are forcing engineers and policymakers to rethink how infrastructure is designed, built, and managed.

MIT News — AI.title: Making machines that can listen
MIT News — AI.description: Professor Paris Smaragdis develops computers with superhuman hearing for applications like speech recognition, music understanding, and environmental monitoring.

MIT News — AI.title: Learner collaborates with MIT peers to develop book of AI insights
MIT News — AI.description: Prabha Jha used her experience with MIT Open Learning’s program for senior executives to develop AI solutions for her employer, Verizon, and to write a book.

MIT News — AI.title: At New York Climate Week 2026, MIT connects with a global network
MIT News — AI.description: A cross-section of the MIT community convened discussions on topics ranging from data centers and super pollutants to agriculture and education.

MIT News — AI.title: At MIT, Martha Minow speaks on sustaining democracy, both by using and overcoming AI
MIT News — AI.description: In Compton Lecture, the distinguished legal scholar warns of potential “loss of the Enlightenment” while suggesting ways innovations can meet our civic and cultural needs.

MIT News — AI.title: Reinforcing the value of human understanding at MIT
MIT News — AI.description: During the School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences’ 75th Anniversary Symposium, President Sally Kornbluth said “MIT has never needed your particular insight and guidance more than we do now.”

MIT News — AI.title: Q&A: How AI came to model the “messy” human mind
MIT News — AI.description: Assistant Professor Benjamin Lindquist studies how engineers deliberately injected randomness into early AI, giving rise to deep-learning models that sometimes hallucinate.

MIT News — AI.title: This design software reimagines everyday objects as self-aware devices
MIT News — AI.description: “X-Hinges” helps design and 3D print items like lamps and gloves with an interactive twist: automatically embedded sensors that perceive and adaptively respond to human contact.

MIT News — AI.title: Why teaching AI about symmetry could make prenatal diagnosis more reliable
MIT News — AI.description: A model developed by researchers at MIT and Boston Children's Hospital adjusts scans on the fly to track fetal movement, potentially sparing families repeat hospital visits.

MIT News — AI.title: Giving AI a “crystal clear” view of the materials world
MIT News — AI.description: New research can help AI models understand crystalline materials in 3D and reason about their properties.

MIT News — AI.title: Fostering community amid Kendall Square’s innovation
MIT News — AI.description: The 18th annual Kendall Square Association Annual Meeting explored how new technologies could be a force for shared prosperity in society.

MIT News — AI.title: State of Supply Chain Sustainability Report finds corporate commitment at record high, but governance lags behind
MIT News — AI.description: MIT's Center for Transportation and Logistics finds sustainability commitments are strong, but governance gaps and external disruptions prevent execution.

MIT News — AI.title: AI model decodes the language cells use to communicate
MIT News — AI.description: A new computational approach reveals how cells communicate to assemble into tissues. This could accelerate stem cell engineering, improve disease models, and inform therapies.
